notes.front: In Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, what are session controls?
notes.back: Access controls that give users only a limited experience inside particular cloud apps, instead of simply letting them in or keeping them out.
notes.explanation: They are a third kind of access control, next to blocking access and granting it.
notes.example: Like a museum that lets you into the gallery but not to photograph the paintings: you are in, with limits on what you do there.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Conditional Access, what is an authentication strength?
notes.back: A grant control that states which combinations of authentication methods users may use to reach a resource.
notes.explanation: Administrators can insist on stronger methods for sensitive resources and still allow lighter ones for everyday access.
notes.example: Like an office where any staff badge opens the front door, but the records room also needs a fingerprint.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are Microsoft Entra roles?
notes.back: Roles that give administrators granular permissions in Microsoft Entra ID, following the principle of least privilege.
notes.explanation: Built-in and custom Entra roles work on concepts similar to the role-based access control used for Azure resources.
notes.example: Like giving a receptionist a key to the post room only, not a master key to the whole building.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra roles allow you to grant granular permissions to your admins, abiding by the principle of least privilege. Microsoft Entra built-in and custom roles operate on concepts similar to those you find in the role-based access control system for Azure resources (Azure roles).

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what can a user with the Global Administrator role do?
notes.back: Use every administrative feature in Microsoft Entra.
notes.explanation: It is one of the most common built-in roles, and like every built-in role its permissions are fixed.
notes.example: Like the caretaker who holds the master key that opens every door in the building.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Built-in roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what can a user with the User Administrator role do?
notes.back: Create and manage every aspect of users and groups, manage support tickets and monitor service health.
notes.explanation: It covers people and group management without the reach over every admin feature that Global Administrator has.
notes.example: Like a personnel clerk who issues and cancels staff passes but cannot change the building alarm system.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Built-in roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what can a user with the Billing Administrator role do?
notes.back: Make purchases, manage subscriptions and support tickets, and monitor service health.
notes.explanation: It is a built-in role, so its bundle of permissions is preconfigured for a task and cannot be edited.
notes.example: Like a firm’s purchasing officer, who orders and pays for services but never manages staff accounts.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Built-in roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what is a custom role?
notes.back: A role definition an organisation builds itself by choosing permissions from a preset list.
notes.explanation: The permissions on offer are the same ones the built-in roles use; the organisation decides which to include.
notes.example: Like choosing your own dishes à la carte from the same kitchen that also serves fixed set menus.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Understand Microsoft Entra role-based access control”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A custom role definition is a collection of permissions that you add from a preset list. These permissions are the same permissions used in the built-in roles.

notes.front: At their simplest, Conditional Access policies are {{c1::if-then statements}}.
notes.back: If-then statements.
notes.explanation: If a user wants to reach a resource, then they must complete an action, such as multifactor authentication.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Conditional Access policies at their simplest are if-then statements: if a user wants to access a resource, then they must complete an action.

notes.front: At what point in a sign-in are Conditional Access policies enforced?
notes.back: After first-factor authentication has been completed.
notes.explanation: Conditional Access isn’t meant to be the frontline defence against denial-of-service attacks, though it can use signals from them to decide access.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Conditional Access policies are enforced after first-factor authentication is completed. Conditional Access isn't intended to be an organization's frontline defense for scenarios like denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, but it can use signals from these events to determine access.

notes.front: Which two goals does Conditional Access help administrators balance?
notes.back: Letting users be productive wherever and whenever; protecting the organisation’s assets.
notes.explanation: Policies apply the right access controls only when needed, keeping the organisation secure without getting in the way of work.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Admins are faced with two primary goals: - Empower users to be productive wherever and whenever - Protect the organization's assets Use Conditional Access policies to apply the right access controls when needed to keep your organization secure and don't interfere with productivity.

notes.front: Conditional Access is Microsoft’s {{c1::Zero Trust}} policy engine.
notes.back: Zero Trust.
notes.explanation: It takes signals from various sources into account when it enforces policy decisions.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Conditional Access is Microsoft's Zero Trust policy engine taking signals from various sources into account when enforcing policy decisions.

notes.front: What two components make up a Conditional Access policy?
notes.back: Assignments (the who, what, where and when) and access controls.
notes.explanation: Assignments describe the situation the policy covers; access controls say how it is enforced once that situation arises.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Conditional Access policy components”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A Conditional Access policy has several assignments configured. How many must a sign-in satisfy to trigger it?
notes.back: All of them: assignments are combined with a logical AND.
notes.explanation: Each extra assignment is one more requirement every sign-in has to match before the policy takes effect.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access assignment can target directory roles, external guests and workload identities?
notes.back: Users.
notes.explanation: It can also target all users, chosen users and groups, and agent identities, which extends Zero Trust to AI workloads.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access assignment picks the cloud apps, user actions or authentication context a policy protects?
notes.back: Target resources.
notes.explanation: User actions include registering security information and registering or joining devices, so a policy can protect an action as well as an app.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access assignment works with trusted address ranges and named locations?
notes.back: Network.
notes.explanation: It decides access by the user’s network or physical location, and admins can include or exclude trusted networks.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access assignment lets administrators combine factors such as device platform and client apps?
notes.back: Conditions.
notes.explanation: Several conditions can be combined in one policy to make it fine-grained.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access condition targets a policy by the operating system on the device?
notes.back: Device platform.
notes.explanation: A policy can then treat, say, phones and desktop computers differently.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access condition looks at the software used to reach cloud apps, such as browsers, mobile apps or desktop clients?
notes.back: Client apps.
notes.explanation: It can be combined with other conditions, such as device platform, for a fine-grained policy.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access condition targets particular devices by their attributes, such as privileged access workstations?
notes.back: Filters for devices.
notes.explanation: It singles out individual devices, where the device platform condition works on the whole operating system.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access condition feeds risk signals from Microsoft Purview into policy decisions?
notes.back: Insider risk.
notes.explanation: Like the other conditions, it can be combined with more conditions in one fine-grained policy.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal lets different policies apply when users try to open particular applications?
notes.back: The application signal.
notes.explanation: Policies can apply to traditional cloud apps, on-premises applications and agent resources.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Common signals”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Trigger different Conditional Access policies when users attempt to access specific applications. - Apply policies to traditional cloud apps, on-premises applications, and agent resources.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access decision is the most restrictive?
notes.back: Block access.
notes.explanation: Grant access is the less restrictive decision, which may still require one or more extra options.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Common decisions”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Block access is the most restrictive decision. - Grant access - A less restrictive decision that might require one or more of the following options:

notes.front: What are the three common kinds of Conditional Access access control?
notes.back: Block access; grant access; session controls.
notes.explanation: Access controls come into play only after a policy’s assignments are satisfied.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two requirements a Conditional Access grant decision can add?
notes.back: Any two of: multifactor authentication; an authentication strength; a device marked as compliant; among others.
notes.explanation: Grant is a less restrictive decision that might require one or more options, or none.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Common decisions”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A less restrictive decision that might require one or more of the following options: - Require multifactor authentication - Require authentication strength - Require the device to be marked as compliant

notes.front: What can Conditional Access App Control do with sensitive documents during a session?
notes.back: Block downloading, cutting, copying and printing them, or require sensitive files to be labelled.
notes.explanation: It is a session control: the user reaches the app, but what they can do there is limited.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which built-in authentication strength accepts a password plus a second factor, such as a text message or voice call?
notes.back: The multifactor authentication strength.
notes.explanation: It allows every combination that satisfies multifactor authentication, password-based ones included.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which built-in authentication strength accepts only methods that satisfy MFA without a password?
notes.back: The passwordless MFA strength.
notes.explanation: Examples include Microsoft Authenticator phone sign-in, FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business and platform credentials.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which built-in authentication strength needs an interaction between the authentication method and the sign-in surface?
notes.back: The phishing-resistant MFA strength.
notes.explanation: Methods that qualify include Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys and multifactor certificate-based authentication.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which two Conditional Access policies could protect generative AI services such as Microsoft 365 Copilot?
notes.back: Any two of: require phishing-resistant MFA for their users; require a compliant device when insider risk is moderate; block access when insider risk is elevated.
notes.explanation: These services can be protected through existing policies that target all resources, or by targeting the AI services’ service principals directly.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Protecting AI services”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra ID licences does Conditional Access require?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.
notes.explanation: Organisations on the free tier can turn on security defaults instead, for a baseline of multifactor authentication.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Licensing”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What happens to existing Conditional Access policies when the licences they need expire?
notes.back: They are not disabled or deleted; admins can view and delete them but can’t update them.
notes.explanation: This graceful state lets customers move away from the policies without a sudden change in their security posture.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “License requirements”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: When the licenses required for Conditional Access expire, policies aren't automatically disabled or deleted. This graceful state lets customers migrate away from Conditional Access policies without a sudden change in their security posture. You can view and delete remaining policies, but you can't update them.

notes.front: Microsoft Entra roles control access to which resources, and through which interface?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra resources such as users, groups and applications, through Microsoft Graph.
notes.explanation: Azure roles, by contrast, control Azure resources such as virtual machines or storage through Azure Resource Management.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra roles control access to Microsoft Entra resources such as users, groups, and applications using the Microsoft Graph API - Azure roles control access to Azure resources such as virtual machines or storage using Azure Resource Management

notes.front: Which two types of role definition does Microsoft Entra ID support?
notes.back: Built-in roles and custom roles.
notes.explanation: Built-in roles come out of the box with a fixed set of permissions, and their definitions can’t be modified.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Understand Microsoft Entra role-based access control”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra ID supports two types of roles definitions: Built-in roles Custom roles Built-in roles are out of box roles that have a fixed set of permissions. These role definitions cannot be modified.

notes.front: What are the two steps to grant permissions with a custom Microsoft Entra role?
notes.back: Create the custom role definition; then assign it to a user through a role assignment.
notes.explanation: Splitting it this way lets you create one role definition and assign it many times at different scopes.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Understand Microsoft Entra role-based access control”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Once you’ve created your custom role definition (or using a built-in role), you can assign it to a user by creating a role assignment. A role assignment grants the user the permissions in a role definition at a specified scope. This two-step process allows you to create a single role definition and assign it many times at different scopes.

notes.front: In a Microsoft Entra role assignment, what does the scope define?
notes.back: The set of Microsoft Entra resources the role member has access to.
notes.explanation: The most common scope covers the whole organisation, but a custom role can also be assigned at an object scope.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Understand Microsoft Entra role-based access control”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A scope defines the set of Microsoft Entra resources the role member has access to. The most common scope is organization-wide (org-wide) scope. A custom role can be assigned at org-wide scope, meaning the role member has the role permissions over all resources in the organization. A custom role can also be assigned at an object scope.

notes.front: What three elements make up a Microsoft Entra role assignment?
notes.back: A security principal; a role definition; a scope.
notes.explanation: The security principal is the identity that gets the permissions: a user, a group or a service principal.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Role assignment”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: At its core, a role assignment consists of three elements: - Security principal - An identity that gets the permissions. It could be a user, group, or a service principal. - Role definition - A collection of permissions. - Scope - A way to constrain where those permissions are applicable.

notes.front: Which licence does each user with a custom Microsoft Entra role assignment need?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra ID P1.
notes.explanation: Using built-in roles in Microsoft Entra ID, by contrast, is free.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “License requirements”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Using built-in roles in Microsoft Entra ID is free. Using custom roles require a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license for every user with a custom role assignment.

notes.front: Why should an admin get the least privileged role that covers their work, rather than Global Administrator?
notes.back: It limits the damage that could be done if their account is compromised.
notes.explanation: The same logic grows with AI services: a compromised over-privileged account lets attackers, and AI tools using its credentials, reach more sensitive data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Only grant the access users need”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which category of Microsoft Entra role grants permissions only over resources inside Microsoft Entra, as Groups Administrator does?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra specific roles.
notes.explanation: User Administrator and Application Administrator are other examples: everything they manage lives in Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Categories of Microsoft Entra roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which category of Microsoft Entra role manages the features of one major Microsoft 365 service, as Exchange Administrator does?
notes.back: Service-specific roles.
notes.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID added these built-in roles so that identity can be managed conveniently across Microsoft 365 services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Categories of Microsoft Entra roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which category of Microsoft Entra role spans several services, as Security Administrator does?
notes.back: Cross-service roles.
notes.explanation: Security Administrator, for example, grants access across several security services within Microsoft 365.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Categories of Microsoft Entra roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Do Microsoft Teams and SharePoint have their own separate role-based access control systems?
notes.back: No; they use Microsoft Entra roles for administrative access.
notes.explanation: Exchange and Intune, by contrast, have developed their own role-based access control systems over time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Categories of Microsoft Entra roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A clinic wants anyone opening its patient-records app to complete multifactor authentication. How would you state that as a Conditional Access if-then policy?
notes.back: If a user wants to access the patient-records app, then they must complete multifactor authentication.
notes.explanation: The “if” names the resource and the “then” names the action the user must complete.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: What is Conditional Access?, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: If a user wants to access an application or service like Microsoft 365, then they must perform multifactor authentication to gain access.

notes.front: A policy targets the Sales group and, under Network, only locations outside the trusted office range. A Sales member signs in from the office. Does the policy apply?
notes.back: No. Every assignment must be satisfied, and the office location fails the network assignment.
notes.explanation: Assignments are combined with a logical AND, so failing one of them means the policy does not trigger.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Assignments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A logistics firm wants its payroll app reachable only from laptops that meet the firm’s device rules. Users who pass must still get in. Which Conditional Access access control fits?
notes.back: D: Grant access, requiring the device to be marked as compliant.
notes.choices:
A) Block access
B) Session controls with sign-in frequency
C) Grant access, requiring a password change
D) Grant access, requiring the device to be marked as compliant
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: block keeps everyone out, including users on compliant laptops. B is wrong: sign-in frequency limits a session but does not check the device. C is wrong: a password change says nothing about the device.
notes.explanation: Grant access can require the device to be marked as compliant, so only laptops meeting the rules get through.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A university’s legal team wants every visiting researcher to accept its conditions before they open a shared research portal. Which grant requirement does that?
notes.back: A: Require terms of use.
notes.choices:
A) Require terms of use
B) Require a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
C) Require a password change
D) Require multifactor authentication
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: visiting researchers’ devices are not the issue. C is wrong: a new password records no acceptance of conditions. D is wrong: multifactor authentication proves identity but asks for no agreement.
notes.explanation: Terms of use is one of the options a grant decision can require before access is given.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A policy says “Require a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device”. Is that a block, grant or session control?
notes.back: A grant control.
notes.explanation: It is one of the requirements administrators can attach when they grant access.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A design agency lets freelancers view its brand files in a cloud app but must stop them downloading or printing sensitive documents. Which kind of Conditional Access control fits?
notes.back: A: Session controls.
notes.choices:
A) Session controls
B) Block access
C) Grant access requiring multifactor authentication
D) Grant access requiring a password change
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: block would stop freelancers viewing the files at all. C is wrong: multifactor authentication checks identity, not what users do after sign-in. D is wrong: a password change does not restrict downloads.
notes.explanation: Session controls let a user in with a limited experience; App Control can block download and print of sensitive documents.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A bank has no staff or customers in one region and wants no sign-ins at all from there, whatever the method. Which decision should its Conditional Access policy apply?
notes.back: A: Block access.
notes.choices:
A) Block access
B) Session controls
C) Grant access requiring multifactor authentication
D) Grant access requiring terms of use
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: session controls let the user in with limits. C is wrong: users who pass multifactor authentication would still get in. D is wrong: accepting terms of use would still let the sign-in through.
notes.explanation: Block access is the most restrictive decision, preventing access under the conditions the policy names.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A pension fund wants administrators of its trading system to use only sign-in methods that interact directly with the sign-in surface, such as FIDO2 security keys. Which built-in authentication strength should it require?
notes.back: D: Phishing-resistant MFA strength.
notes.choices:
A) Multifactor authentication strength
B) Passwordless MFA strength
C) Security defaults
D) Phishing-resistant MFA strength
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: it allows a password plus a text message or call. B is wrong: it drops the password but is not defined by that interaction with the sign-in surface. C is wrong: security defaults are a baseline setting, not an authentication strength.
notes.explanation: That strength restricts access to methods needing an interaction between the method and the sign-in surface.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A user signs in with a password and then approves a push notification. Which built-in authentication strength does that combination fall under?
notes.back: The multifactor authentication strength only.
notes.explanation: The passwordless strength excludes any method that needs a password, and a password plus a second factor is the multifactor pattern.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: None of the three built-in authentication strengths matches the exact set of methods a council wants to allow. What can its administrators do?
notes.back: Create a custom authentication strength that allows exactly that combination of methods.
notes.explanation: Custom strengths exist for organisations whose requirements the built-in ones don’t match.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A small charity uses the free tier of Microsoft Entra ID and wants a baseline of multifactor authentication without buying licences. What should it use?
notes.back: D: Security defaults.
notes.choices:
A) An authentication strength
B) A Conditional Access policy requiring multifactor authentication
C) A custom role
D) Security defaults
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: authentication strengths are a Conditional Access grant control, so they need the same licences. B is wrong: Conditional Access needs P1 or P2 licences. C is wrong: a custom role grants admin permissions and needs P1 itself.
notes.explanation: Conditional Access needs P1 or P2 licences; security defaults give free-tier organisations baseline multifactor authentication.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Licensing”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: At a school trust, one staff member creates staff accounts, manages groups and raises support tickets, and does nothing else in Microsoft Entra ID. Which built-in role follows least privilege?
notes.back: D: User Administrator.
notes.choices:
A) Global Administrator
B) Billing Administrator
C) No role; make the staff member a guest
D) User Administrator
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: it opens every admin feature, far more than the job needs. B is wrong: it handles purchases and subscriptions, not users and groups. C is wrong: a guest gets no permission to manage users.
notes.explanation: Someone who mostly manages users should get User Administrator rather than Global Administrator, limiting the harm a compromised account could do.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Only grant the access users need”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A finance officer must buy subscriptions and follow service health, without touching user accounts. Which built-in Microsoft Entra role fits best?
notes.back: A: Billing Administrator.
notes.choices:
A) Billing Administrator
B) User Administrator
C) Global Administrator
D) A custom role holding every permission
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: it manages users and groups, which the officer must not touch. C is wrong: it reaches every admin feature. D is wrong: a role holding every permission defeats least privilege.
notes.explanation: Billing Administrator covers purchases, subscriptions, support tickets and service health, and nothing about users.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Built-in roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A consultant must manage the settings of one enterprise application and nothing else in the directory. No built-in role is narrow enough. What should the admin do?
notes.back: D: Create a custom role and assign it scoped to that enterprise application.
notes.choices:
A) Assign an Azure role on the subscription
B) Assign Global Administrator for a week
C) Assign User Administrator
D) Create a custom role and assign it scoped to that enterprise application
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: Azure roles cover Azure resources, not Microsoft Entra objects. B is wrong: it grants every admin feature, far beyond one app. C is wrong: it manages users and groups, not one enterprise application’s settings.
notes.explanation: A role can be scoped to a single Microsoft Entra resource, such as one enterprise application, instead of the whole tenant.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Scope”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: When you assign a role, you specify one of the following types of scope: - Tenant - Administrative unit - Microsoft Entra resource If you specify a Microsoft Entra resource as a scope, it can be one of the following: - Microsoft Entra groups - Enterprise applications - Application registrations

notes.front: An engineer needs to restart virtual machines in a subscription but must not manage users. Which system should grant that permission?
notes.back: A: Azure RBAC, through an Azure role.
notes.choices:
A) Azure RBAC, through an Azure role
B) Global Administrator
C) A Conditional Access grant control
D) A Microsoft Entra role such as User Administrator
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: it covers Microsoft Entra admin features and breaks least privilege. C is wrong: Conditional Access decides how people sign in, not what they may change. D is wrong: User Administrator manages users and groups, not virtual machines.
notes.explanation: Azure roles control Azure resources such as virtual machines; Microsoft Entra roles control users, groups and applications.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Difference between Microsoft Entra RBAC and Azure RBAC”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Creating user accounts in the directory: is that governed by Microsoft Entra roles or by Azure roles?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra roles.
notes.explanation: Users, groups and applications are Microsoft Entra resources, the kind Entra roles control; Azure roles cover resources such as storage.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Difference between Microsoft Entra RBAC and Azure RBAC”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Compliance Administrator manages compliance settings in Microsoft Purview, Exchange and other services. Which category of Microsoft Entra role is it?
notes.back: A cross-service role.
notes.explanation: Its reach spans several services rather than living in Microsoft Entra alone or in one Microsoft 365 service.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Categories of Microsoft Entra roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does blocking access differ from applying session controls in Conditional Access?
notes.back: Block keeps the user out entirely; session controls let the user in but limit what they can do inside the app.
notes.explanation: Block is the most restrictive decision, while session controls enable a limited experience in specific cloud apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Access controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does requiring an authentication strength differ from simply requiring multifactor authentication?
notes.back: Requiring MFA accepts any method combination that satisfies MFA; a strength names which combinations are allowed.
notes.explanation: That is how a sensitive resource can demand, say, phishing-resistant methods while everyday apps accept any MFA.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Conditional Access, “Authentication strengths”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does a custom Microsoft Entra role differ from a built-in one?
notes.back: A built-in role’s permissions are fixed; a custom role holds the permissions you choose from the same preset list.
notes.explanation: Custom roles give flexibility when no built-in admin role grants exactly the access needed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC), “Custom roles”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Can permissions from Microsoft Entra roles be used in Azure custom roles?
notes.back: No, and Azure role permissions can’t be used in Microsoft Entra custom roles either.
notes.explanation: The two systems use similar role definitions and role assignments, yet their permissions stay separate.
notes.source: Microsoft Entra documentation: Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID, “Overview of role-based access control in Microsoft Entra ID”
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Both systems contain similarly used role definitions and role assignments. However, Microsoft Entra role permissions can't be used in Azure custom roles and vice versa.
